title: World map outline
subject: PSHE
unit: Spring 2: Who likes chocolate? Global trade, media and stereotyping
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 11 (World map outline (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 11: Trade across the world. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Mark where your food was grown, then draw its journey to the UK with arrows. Label the country and the way it travelled (ship, plane, lorry).

keywords.def: goods sent out of a country

questions.q: A bar travels from Ghana to the UK via Europe. Name the import and export at each step.
questions.a: Ghana exports cocoa; Europe imports cocoa and exports chocolate; the UK imports chocolate.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: choose a food from your kitchen, find where it was grown, and draw its journey on the world map outline.
questions.a: A labelled journey with import and export marked.

questions.q: Extend: give one advantage and one disadvantage of food travelling far.
questions.a: Advantage: variety and jobs; disadvantage: fuel use and pollution.

questions.q: Cocoa arriving in the UK from Ghana is a UK ...
questions.a: A) import. Goods coming in are imports.
goods sent out of a country
options: goods sent out of a country

questions.q: Think again: Your breakfast may have travelled thousands of miles. Is that good, bad, or both?
questions.a: Both: we get variety and farmers earn, but transport uses fuel and farmers may be paid unfairly.
